secret.unlockText: After the first credits roll, a pencilled invitation appears under the brass bell.

open.name: Gojo Satoru
open.text: I've got a student waiting for his face back.

open.name: Sukuna
open.text: Then he'll have to wait in line.

gojo.name: Gojo Satoru
gojo.text: Look at me. You still in there, kid?

sukuna.name: Sukuna
sukuna.text: You can take attendance again tomorrow.

open.name: Gojo Satoru
open.text: That face has missed enough class.

open.name: Ryomen Sukuna Shinjuku
open.text: I found a more demanding use for his hands.

gojo.name: Gojo Satoru
gojo.text: I'll take it from here. He's done plenty.

sukuna_shinjuku.name: Ryomen Sukuna Shinjuku
sukuna_shinjuku.text: Concern makes even your aim predictable.

open.name: Gojo Satoru
open.text: Different history. Same expression when the cheque comes.

open.name: Alternate Sukuna
open.text: In my history someone else paid.

gojo.name: Gojo Satoru
gojo.text: Split it three ways? Didn't think so.

open.name: Satoru Gojo Shinjuku
open.text: Funny seeing you in this one again.

open.name: Sukuna
open.text: You preferred the other brat?

gojo_shinjuku.name: Satoru Gojo Shinjuku
gojo_shinjuku.text: They're my students. Both of them.

sukuna.name: Sukuna
sukuna.text: You looked for the boy first. I noticed.

open.name: Satoru Gojo Shinjuku
open.text: That street looks smaller from down here.

open.name: Ryomen Sukuna Shinjuku
open.text: It only had to be wide enough for two.

gojo_shinjuku.name: Satoru Gojo Shinjuku
gojo_shinjuku.text: This minute belongs to another history. I'll take it.

sukuna_shinjuku.name: Ryomen Sukuna Shinjuku
sukuna_shinjuku.text: You spent every inch of that street. Good.

open.name: Satoru Gojo Shinjuku
open.text: Haven't met this version. Any pleasant surprises?

open.name: Alternate Sukuna
open.text: You've had every pleasant surprise you'll get.

gojo_shinjuku.name: Satoru Gojo Shinjuku
gojo_shinjuku.text: Turns out I still enjoy a first meeting.

alt_sukuna.name: Alternate Sukuna
alt_sukuna.text: There. Something new to remember me by.

open.name: Naruto
open.text: I know that look. You're about to leave without telling anybody.

open.name: Sasuke
open.text: You always were loud enough to cover a goodbye.

naruto.name: Naruto
naruto.text: Sit down a minute. I'll be quiet. Promise.

open.name: Naruto
open.text: Whoa. How long were you gone this time?

open.name: Sasuke Adult
open.text: Long enough to miss how annoying that sounds.

sasuke_adult.name: Sasuke Adult
sasuke_adult.text: Keep asking. One day I'll answer sooner.

open.name: Naruto
open.text: Does teaching make you give homework now?

open.name: Sasuke Sensei
open.text: Yes. Find my blind side.

naruto.name: Naruto
naruto.text: Found it! Do I get extra ramen?

sasuke_sensei.name: Sasuke Sensei
sasuke_sensei.text: Again. This time keep your hands up when you celebrate.

open.name: Naruto Seventh Hokage
open.text: I can clear my afternoon.

open.name: Sasuke
open.text: Planning to bring me in personally, Hokage?

naruto_seventh.name: Naruto Seventh Hokage
naruto_seventh.text: Nah. Wanted the walk back with you.

sasuke.name: Sasuke
sasuke.text: A whole afternoon. You must mean it.

open.name: Naruto Seventh Hokage
open.text: I signed your travel papers. Couldn't work in a visit home?

open.name: Sasuke Adult
open.text: Couldn't put what I saw in a letter.

naruto_seventh.name: Naruto Seventh Hokage
naruto_seventh.text: All right. Now you can tell me in person.

sasuke_adult.name: Sasuke Adult
sasuke_adult.text: Next time use the good paper. Yours dissolved in the rain.

open.name: Naruto Seventh Hokage
open.text: Which one of us is explaining the broken monument?

open.name: Sasuke Sensei
open.text: The one whose face is carved in it.

naruto_seventh.name: Naruto Seventh Hokage
naruto_seventh.text: Fine. You get the parents' meeting.

sasuke_sensei.name: Sasuke Sensei
sasuke_sensei.text: Keep the hat on. It lends the story dignity.

open.name: Kakashi
open.text: I brought flowers. Never worked out what else to bring.

open.name: Obito
open.text: You could've brought an honest answer.

obito.name: Obito
obito.text: Leave them here. Flowers won't hurt anybody.

open.name: Kakashi
open.text: You put on an extra voice when the mask slips.

open.name: Tobi
open.text: What a suspicious thing to notice, sir!

kakashi.name: Kakashi
kakashi.text: You can stop laughing now. It's just us.

tobi.name: Tobi
tobi.text: Funny. You listened right through it.

open.name: Kakashi ANBU
open.text: Identify yourself. Hands where I can see them.

open.name: Obito
open.text: You used to know them by the goggles they held.

obito.name: Obito
obito.text: Too young to recognize me. Old enough to look tired.

open.name: Kakashi ANBU
open.text: A mask is equipment. Yours is talking too much.

open.name: Tobi
open.text: Oh, I can be VERY professional.

kakashi_anbu.name: Kakashi ANBU
kakashi_anbu.text: First quiet second since you arrived.

tobi.name: Tobi
tobi.text: That uniform taught you terrible manners.

open.name: Kakashi Kamui
open.text: We keep meeting on opposite sides of this same hole.

open.name: Obito
open.text: Then show me what you found on yours.

obito.name: Obito
obito.text: It looked smaller from where you stood.

open.name: Kakashi Kamui
open.text: I know where the missing part goes.

open.name: Tobi
open.text: Maybe it just takes a lovely holiday!

kakashi_war.name: Kakashi Kamui
kakashi_war.text: The joke was better before I knew you meant it.

tobi.name: Tobi
tobi.text: You nearly laughed. I'll count it.

open.name: Itachi
open.text: You should have had a life outside the story I told you.

open.name: Sasuke
open.text: I had to grow up inside it first.

itachi.name: Itachi
itachi.text: Ask the question again. I'll stay.

sasuke.name: Sasuke
sasuke.text: I wanted an answer. I still do.

open.name: Itachi
open.text: You carry less anger in that hand.

open.name: Sasuke Adult
open.text: It's usually carrying something home.

itachi.name: Itachi
itachi.text: I'm glad you found something worth bringing.

sasuke_adult.name: Sasuke Adult
sasuke_adult.text: There was a place at the table. You should know that.

open.name: Itachi
open.text: What do your students know of me?

open.name: Sasuke Sensei
open.text: Enough to ask better questions than I did.

itachi.name: Itachi
itachi.text: Perhaps they will teach you something too.

sasuke_sensei.name: Sasuke Sensei
sasuke_sensei.text: They already have. I let them see when I'm wrong.

open.name: Mark Grayson
open.text: If I get up again, are you gonna tell me it's because I'm yours?

open.name: Omni-Man
open.text: I was going to tell you to get your feet under you, son.

invincible.name: Mark Grayson
invincible.text: Got 'em under me. Picked where to stand, too.

omniman_viltrum.name: Omni-Man
omniman_viltrum.text: I wish my own father had let me talk this long.

open.name: Homelander
open.text: Let's hear it, big guy. Who do the people want?

open.name: Superman
open.text: There's a woman under the balcony. Let's ask if she can walk.

superman.name: Superman
superman.text: She can walk. You can help carry her chair.

open.name: Batman
open.text: I've accounted for what you'll do if the sun goes red.

open.name: Superman
open.text: Did you account for what I'd do if you fell?

batman.name: Batman
batman.text: Yes. That's why I brought two lines.

superman.name: Superman
superman.text: One of these days you'll just ask me to catch you.

open.name: Ichigo
open.text: I've got somewhere to be. Can we walk and do this?

open.name: Zaraki Kenpachi
open.text: Finally. Somebody with a good idea.

ichigo.name: Ichigo
ichigo.text: You took us three blocks the wrong way!

zaraki.name: Zaraki Kenpachi
zaraki.text: You were in front. How's it my fault?

open.name: Ichigo
open.text: I heard that thing from the next street.

open.name: Zaraki Shikai
open.text: She wanted you to hear her.

ichigo.name: Ichigo
ichigo.text: Tell her she's got a hell of a voice.

zaraki_shikai.name: Zaraki Shikai
zaraki_shikai.text: Tell her yourself. She can hear you.

open.name: Goku
open.text: Bet I can tell which shoulder you're gonna lead with.

open.name: Vegeta
open.text: Then why haven't you moved, Kakarot?

goku.name: Goku
goku.text: Wrong shoulder. Lucky I've got a chin.

vegeta.name: Vegeta
vegeta.text: That's what studying you for years buys me.

open.name: Goku
open.text: So is this practice or am I saving something?

open.name: Beerus
open.text: It was practice until you stepped on my lunch.

goku.name: Goku
goku.text: Uh. I know a place that does noodles.

open.name: Goku
open.text: My face looks weird when you smile with it.

open.name: Goku Black
open.text: You never understood what that body could express.

goku.name: Goku
goku.text: Yeah. It can get back up for somebody.

goku_black.name: Goku Black
goku_black.text: Feel how quickly flesh believes its rightful master.

open.name: Ben Tennyson
open.text: Please tell me you picked up fries on the way.

open.name: Albedo
open.text: I refuse to share the consequences of your metabolism.

ben10.name: Ben Tennyson
ben10.text: You ate them in the car, didn't you?

albedo.name: Albedo
albedo.text: I have retained the receipt. You owe me.

open.name: Ben Tennyson
open.text: You've got a whole collection of hobbies and you still want my watch?

open.name: Vilgax
open.text: I collect victories. There is an irritating gap.

vilgax.name: Vilgax
vilgax.text: You were always the least valuable part of the set.

open.name: Rick Sanchez
open.text: I had a whole speech for this. Guess I used it up in traffic.

open.name: Rick Prime
open.text: Keep going. I love hearing what you've been doing with my time.

rick.name: Rick Sanchez
rick.text: Huh. Still have to drive back.

open.name: Light Yagami
open.text: You look exhausted. How long have you been waiting for me to slip?

open.name: L
open.text: Long enough to know you checked my face before you checked the door.

l_ryuuzaki.name: L
l_ryuuzaki.text: Curious. Even now you want to decide when I rest.

open.name: Zoro
open.text: That leg's pretty high for a guy carrying hot soup.

open.name: Sanji
open.text: That sword's pretty low for a guy about to lose a toe.

zoro.name: Zoro
zoro.text: Didn't spill any. I'll give you that.

open.name: Zoro
open.text: Captain. Want me to cut the gap wider?

open.name: Luffy
open.text: I wanna know what's on the other side of YOU first!

zoro.name: Zoro
zoro.text: Nothing back there but lunch. Hey. Wait.

open.name: Sanji
open.text: You ate the emergency rations and the box they came in.

open.name: Luffy
open.text: The box smelled like meat.

open.name: Killua
open.text: You do that little smile before you try to scare somebody.

open.name: Hisoka
open.text: How observant. What comes after the smile?

killua.name: Killua
killua.text: Usually? You look around for an audience.

hisoka.name: Hisoka
hisoka.text: My, my. You watched my eyes the entire time.

open.name: Killua
open.text: Do you return things when you're finished borrowing them?

open.name: Chrollo
open.text: You've already decided which hand to watch.

killua.name: Killua
killua.text: I watched what you wanted me to ignore.

chrollo.name: Chrollo
chrollo.text: You have a hunter's patience when it matters.

open.name: Samurai Red
open.text: A commander takes responsibility for an order. Name yours.

open.name: Krybot
open.text: Order origin withheld.

samurai_red_ranger.name: Samurai Red
samurai_red_ranger.text: Then I'll take responsibility for stopping it.

open.name: Gold Samurai
open.text: You take requests? I've got a number that'll blow a fuse.

open.name: Krybot
open.text: Audio channel reserved.

open.name: Green Samurai
open.text: Bet you can't tell which way I'm going either.

open.name: Krybot
open.text: Trajectory inconsistent.

open.name: Mighty Morphin Rangers
open.text: Count again. You missed the ones covering our backs.

open.name: Krybot
open.text: Counting individual targets.

open.name: S.P.D. Rangers
open.text: Identify your issuing authority. We're recording this.

open.name: Krybot
open.text: Recording prohibited.

spd_rangers.name: S.P.D. Rangers
spd_rangers.text: Good thing we kept the receipt.

open.name: Ninja Storm CGPT
open.text: See that afterimage? Tell it the rules.

open.name: Krybot
open.text: Infraction registered at two locations.

ninja_storm_cgpt.name: Ninja Storm CGPT
ninja_storm_cgpt.text: Send both tickets to the wind.

open.name: Dino Thunder Rangers
open.text: You might want to sample that noise again. That's the whole herd.

open.name: Krybot
open.text: Single threat authorized.

open.name: Ninja Storm Squad
open.text: Three footprints. How many of us can you actually see?

open.name: Krybot
open.text: One. Zero. One.

open.name: Ninja Storm Rangers
open.text: Heads up. We're crossing on the whistle.

open.name: Krybot
open.text: Waiting for acoustic signal.

ninja_storm_rangers.name: Ninja Storm Rangers
ninja_storm_rangers.text: Never said who was blowing it.

open.name: Saitama
open.text: One clean touch. That way there's still a building after.

open.name: Genos
open.text: Should I calculate the safe radius for a clean touch?

saitama.name: Saitama
saitama.text: You can put the tape measure away.

genos.name: Genos
genos.text: Sensei, it appears you were holding the wrong end.

open.name: Hinata
open.text: I know what it costs to stand in front of people who once looked away.

open.name: Gaara
open.text: It costs less when somebody stands beside you.

hinata.name: Hinata
hinata.text: I can see the opening now.

gaara.name: Gaara
gaara.text: There's room behind the sand. Come through.

open.name: Naruto
open.text: You gave me a question I couldn't answer with my fists.

open.name: Pain
open.text: And still you arrive ready to fight.

pain.name: Pain
pain.text: Stay, then. Hear the silence you leave.

open.name: Yuta Okkotsu
open.text: Remember the first time you showed me how to hold this?

open.name: Maki Zenin
open.text: I remember how close you came to cutting your own ear.

yuta.name: Yuta Okkotsu
yuta.text: Was my grip better that time?

maki.name: Maki Zenin
maki.text: Your ears are still attached. Good start.

open.name: Gojo Satoru
open.text: I'd remember that footwork anywhere.

open.name: Toji Fushiguro
open.text: Pity you can't send me a referral fee.

open.name: Sasuke
open.text: How many people knew what my brother carried?

open.name: Shisui Fallen
open.text: Fewer than should have. I was one.

sasuke.name: Sasuke
sasuke.text: That's one honest answer, at least.

shisui_fallen.name: Shisui Fallen
shisui_fallen.text: If you want the rest, I'll sit.

open.name: Netero
open.text: Shall we see whose hand reaches the teapot first?

open.name: Beerus
open.text: You warmed the pot. I may actually enjoy this.

open.name: Frozone
open.text: Kid, those turns are banked for a reason.

open.name: Dash
open.text: Yeah. To see how high I can get!

frozone.name: Frozone
frozone.text: Your mother can have that conversation.

dash_parr.name: Dash
dash_parr.text: Did you see the landing, though?

open.name: Spider-Man
open.text: Do your goggles survive faceplants? Asking for scientific reasons.

open.name: Mark Grayson
open.text: Mostly. The bad news is what happens to the nose.

spiderman.name: Spider-Man
spiderman.text: I am withdrawing my patent application.

invincible.name: Mark Grayson
invincible.text: I'll send you the name of my tailor.

open.name: Baki Hanma
open.text: What do you learn by staying inside those ropes?

open.name: Ippo
open.text: How far my own hands can reach.

baki.name: Baki Hanma
baki.text: Funny. I felt the ropes even out here.

ippo.name: Ippo
ippo.text: I think I moved you half a step.

open.name: Jesus
open.text: Whose name would you write if the page could feel your hand?

open.name: Light Yagami
open.text: Someone must answer for what people do.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.text: Begin with the name you answer to.

light.name: Light Yagami
light.text: Why didn't you ask me to spare you?

open.name: Ghostface
open.text: Pick up. I left a clue in the question.

open.name: L
open.text: You inhaled twice. You've practised sounding out of breath.

l_ryuuzaki.name: L
l_ryuuzaki.text: I wanted the sound of the room behind you.

open.name: Omololu
open.text: Which one of us forgot to unplug the bell?

open.name: Dseyl
open.text: Which one soldered it straight into the wall?

omololu.name: Omololu
omololu.text: Okay. You can have that one.

dseyl.name: Dseyl
dseyl.text: I'm putting a plug on the next one.

open.name: Robin
open.text: You trained me to see the opening. You hate when I use it.

open.name: Batman
open.text: I hate when you tell me first.

robin.name: Robin
robin.text: This time I told you afterward.

batman.name: Batman
batman.text: That's better. Next time keep your elbow in.

open.name: Dark Vegeta
open.text: I can hear every order you swallowed.

open.name: Vegeta
open.text: Then hear what I do with the next one.

vegeta_dark.name: Dark Vegeta
vegeta_dark.text: I broke the voice. The strength stayed in my hands.

vegeta.name: Vegeta
vegeta.text: You dropped your guard the instant you heard your own voice.

open.name: Aoi Todo
open.text: Brother! That bell just interrupted your best combination.

open.name: Yuji Itadori
open.text: It's got lousy rhythm. Start me on the offbeat.

aoi_todo.name: Aoi Todo
aoi_todo.text: Now that was an answer worth waiting for!

yuji.name: Yuji Itadori
yuji.text: Left, right, and somebody else gets to go home. Nice combo.

open.name: Kasumi Miwa
open.text: My sword's shadow is still in its sheath. Is that yours?

open.name: Megumi Fushiguro
open.text: Mine would have better manners. Probably.

miwa.name: Kasumi Miwa
miwa.text: I drew before the shadow. I'm writing that down.

megumi_fushiguro.name: Megumi Fushiguro
megumi_fushiguro.text: Your footing gave it away. The shadow never moved its heel.

open.name: Hiromi Higuruma
open.text: Who certified your list of volunteers?

open.name: Light Yagami
open.text: People who are saved rarely object afterward.

higuruma.name: Hiromi Higuruma
higuruma.text: I'll call the ones who objected first.

light.name: Light Yagami
light.text: You gave them a hearing. I had the verdict ready.

open.name: Tobirama
open.text: Brother, you gave the door the village password.

open.name: Hashirama
open.text: It asked if I had family inside. I do.

tobirama.name: Tobirama
tobirama.text: I've changed the password. You may still visit.

hashirama.name: Hashirama
hashirama.text: Your exact words were “open to family.” Come in.

open.name: Minato
open.text: Sensei, this seal loops back to the dedication on your book.

open.name: Jiraiya
open.text: Finally, somebody read the dedication!

minato.name: Minato
minato.text: There was good advice under the coffee stain.

jiraiya.name: Jiraiya
jiraiya.text: Your handwriting got smaller. Your heart didn't.

open.name: Madara
open.text: Six faces, and someone else has chosen where they stand.

open.name: Six Paths of Pain
open.text: You should recognize the arrangement.

madara.name: Madara
madara.text: A good view from up there. A poor place to put down roots.

six_paths_pain.name: Six Paths of Pain
six_paths_pain.text: Even you felt it when one body fell alone.

open.name: Sakura
open.text: That smile. How many patients are you worried about?

open.name: Shinobu
open.text: Every bed in the room. You counted too, I see.

sakura.name: Sakura
sakura.text: I'll take this shift. Go ahead and let your face rest.

shinobu.name: Shinobu
shinobu.text: Thank you for showing me which wrist you favour. May I dress it?

open.name: Zenitsu
open.text: I can hear you breathing inside that barrel.

open.name: Inosuke
open.text: Then quit telling the barrel where I am!

zenitsu.name: Zenitsu
zenitsu.text: You can come out. I think I scared myself enough for both of us.

inosuke.name: Inosuke
inosuke.text: I beat the hearing guy at hiding! Somebody tell the barrel!

open.name: Rengoku
open.text: There are passengers behind me. Will you stand for them?

open.name: Nezuko
open.text: [She plants both feet across the carriage door and nods.]

rengoku.name: Rengoku
rengoku.text: Excellent! There was never any doubt which way you faced.

nezuko.name: Nezuko
nezuko.text: [She lifts a fallen ticket and puts it back in his hand.]

open.name: Kevin Levin
open.text: Before you say it, I only touched the one panel.

open.name: Gwen
open.text: I was going to say that panel is touching you back.

kevin_levin.name: Kevin Levin
kevin_levin.text: I got my hand loose. How about a little credit?

gwen.name: Gwen
gwen.text: You get credit for telling me which panel. Next time, sooner.

open.name: The Flash
open.text: Did you seriously put a bell on that arrow?

open.name: Green Arrow
open.text: Yeah. I'd like to hear you catch this one.

flash.name: The Flash
flash.text: Caught it. The little tune was a nice touch.

green_arrow.name: Green Arrow
green_arrow.text: You listened for the bell. The ribbon got there first.

open.name: Cyborg
open.text: If you turn into a mouse again, stay out of the wiring.

open.name: Beast Boy
open.text: That was one time! And I found the loose cable.

cyborg.name: Cyborg
cyborg.text: Diagnostic complete. One green mouse, officially grounded.

beast_boy.name: Beast Boy
beast_boy.text: You owe your whole network a very small piece of cheese.

open.name: Raven
open.text: If you hear my voice through that door, ask how I take my tea.

open.name: Starfire
open.text: I remember. In silence, with a second cup for me.

raven.name: Raven
raven.text: I put the kettle on. You know where your cup is.

starfire.name: Starfire
starfire.text: The voice said you drink alone. That was its mistake.

open.name: Soldier Boy
open.text: They paid somebody to stitch muscles into that thing?

open.name: Homelander
open.text: They paid somebody to teach you to read the cue cards.

soldier_boy.name: Soldier Boy
soldier_boy.text: Camera's off. Get up under your own steam.

homelander.name: Homelander
homelander.text: Smile. This'll look great in the tribute reel.

open.name: Saiki Kusuo
open.text: [Telepathy] Someone is counting heads. Want to disappoint them?

open.name: Violet
open.text: For once, disappearing sounds like a group project.

saiki.name: Saiki Kusuo
saiki.text: [Telepathy] We got everyone out. I'll take an absent mark.

violet.name: Violet
violet.text: You saved me a seat. Nobody ever remembers to do that.

open.name: Syndrome
open.text: Try the rescue again. This time look up at my camera.

open.name: Mr. Incredible
open.text: I looked down. There was a kid under the rig.

syndrome.name: Syndrome
syndrome.text: You did exactly what I predicted. Why aren't they clapping?

mr_incredible.name: Mr. Incredible
mr_incredible.text: You wanted a close-up. Help me lift this and you've got one.

open.name: Elastigirl
open.text: Can your register tell me whose hand I just grabbed?

open.name: Enoch
open.text: No. It can tell you who was last seen reaching.

elastigirl.name: Elastigirl
elastigirl.text: Well, now you can pencil in “home with family.”

enoch.name: Enoch
enoch.text: I put the pencil down and reached. That got a better answer.

open.name: Jason Voorhees
open.text: [He turns the ringing phone over. The wire has already been cut.]

open.name: Ghostface
open.text: All right. Tough audience. How about a silent picture?

jason.name: Jason Voorhees
jason.text: [He sets the receiver in the empty chair. The caller backs away.]

ghostface.name: Ghostface
ghostface.text: You listened for the phone. I was behind the camera.

open.name: Mayuri
open.text: One little vial would settle whether this gate can bleed.

open.name: Byakuya
open.text: You asked the gate. You neglected to ask its keeper.

mayuri.name: Mayuri
mayuri.text: How irritating. The control specimen has filed an objection.

byakuya.name: Byakuya
byakuya.text: The vial is empty. You have your answer.

open.name: Buggy
open.text: Tickets to see a genius! Even your guys lined up!

open.name: Arlong
open.text: Look down, clown. They're standing in my toll queue.

buggy.name: Buggy
buggy.text: Two lines and I'm collecting at the front of both!

arlong.name: Arlong
arlong.text: I charge by the piece. Count your fingers.

open.name: Isshiki Otsutsuki
open.text: You spend your life answering when strangers call.

open.name: Naruto
open.text: Yeah. Funny how they keep showing up for me too.

isshiki.name: Isshiki Otsutsuki
isshiki.text: At last, a moment's quiet. Why do I still hear them?

naruto.name: Naruto
naruto.text: We answered separately. Try fitting that in your hand.

lines.text: What happens if I break the testing machine?
You get to carry it upstairs.
Now that's an incentive to pull a punch.
My shadow went through the barrier before I did.
How many sets of tracks on the other side?
One. Whatever owns it is standing very still.
Your door keeps collecting fear. We get called out for that.
How do you know when it's full?
When it starts making house calls.
I recognize a seal drawn from the outside.
Ours has a latch on both faces.
Then explain why only one side has scratches.
When I power up, the chain on your gate rattles.
The dead can feel it too. Give them a warning.
Three taps before the next one. Like this?
Your meter stopped going up. Need a bigger one?
The dial unscrewed itself. Hold this spring.
Huh. Guess it found its limit before we did.
There are souls on the register with no way to sign.
I can lend them the bell.
Leave it low. One of them is a child.
That passenger's pulse changes every fourth beat.
Bait usually has a pattern. What's behind the seat?
A second passenger trying to breathe for two.
The sun rose twice in that window.
One sunrise belongs to the carriage ahead.
Pull the shade until we know which one reaches this seat.
Your door set a condition and offered a reward.
It promised safe passage. What's the catch?
It never said safe passage for whom.
Which one of these doors leads back to our lunch?
The one with the grease on the handle. Science, right?
Good. You're washing the plates when we get back.
A compass shouldn't point straight down at your wrist.
Something down there thinks my watch is calling it.
Take the line around your waist. We'll find out together.
Someone put a price on the tide.
The receipt says you can take it with you.
Ever tried fitting the sea in your pocket?
Oh good, another device with one big friendly button.
You can tell where to put your thumb. That's called design.
It's also how I lost my last thumb.
Your prototype shipped with a recording that says yes?
It was supposed to test an empty room.
Great. You've invented a room nobody can leave a bad review for.
The dial's green, but it isn't offering a transformation.
That's our emergency lamp reflected in the glass.
Then the person we need is under the dial. Help me lift it.
How many people answered when you called home?
Everybody talked at once. Best sound I ever heard.
Same thing happens when we call the team.
The alarm's tuned to our communicators. Can you hear it?
So can everyone taking the maths exam.
We'll take attendance outside.
Anybody in that classroom need a rescue?
The kid in the back would like a pencil.
Finally, an emergency where we packed exactly the right thing.
There's a kid counting the seconds between impacts.
I told him it's thunder. He asked where the rain went.
Smart kid. Let's get his sky back.
How far can you carry that roof?
Past the people underneath. Anything after that is a bonus.
On three, then. Save your breath for the lift.
That camera has the only clear view of the exit.
Yeah, that's why they sold the space in front of it.
Let's give the people watching directions.
Who holds the second key to your lab?
We cut three. I thought that made us careful.
Tell me who can turn one down.
First time getting thrown through somebody else's skyline?
I've got a preferred landing shoulder.
I was hoping for a recommendation on cheap windows.
You signed the rescue photo before the rescue?
Publicity likes to be ready.
Great. Put the evacuation instructions on the back.
I found a wire labelled “temporary.” How old is it?
Older than the machine it's holding up.
Oh, good. We went to the same engineering school.
Do you ever wonder who has to catch everything you drop?
There's a whole department for that.
I met the department. It's one guy with a broom.
You built something big enough to scare my people.
I built it small enough to fit on my desk.
Same thing, depending on who's sitting there.
This waiver covers any casualties on camera.
You're holding it upside down.
Nobody ever reads these anyway. Why'd you take my pen?
[The phone rings. The caller waits for a name.]
A name is the one thing I won't give a stranger.
[A pencil scratches three times inside the receiver.]
[A floorboard bends under a motionless figure.]
All that weight on the front foot. You're waiting for me.
[The figure takes its heel off the floor.]
[Two knocks sound from the far side of the canvas.]
In the gym we knock back so you know somebody's here.
[This time the knocks come from under the stool.]
[A latch scrapes shut in the dark.]
I hear someone on the other side. Make room.
[One hand slips through the gap and holds it open.]
[An unplugged telephone gives a busy signal.]
Our lab used that tone when a door was occupied.
[The tone stops. There is breathing on the line.]
I could predict the result from your last ten fights.
Could you tell me which one made me come back?
That detail seems to be missing from the record.
Nine on the clock. What evidence do you need for ten?
I'd like to see the fighter's eyes before I count.
Interesting. The board never asks anyone to look.
Suppose the person beyond that door deserves punishment.
Would you hear that person's voice before you decide?
That makes the decision rather harder.
Who supplied the signature on this page?
The machine did. Look at the dent underneath.
The same dent on every sheet. One signature printed a thousand times.
Somebody drew a ring without a corner to rest in.
Then I'll be your corner when the bell goes.
Do that and I might actually listen this time.
You saw me lower my guard. Why didn't you come through?
You were waiting for someone to hit you. Who taught you to wait?
Now there's a question that could put me on the floor.
This plate only notices me when I throw a punch.
Step on the seam between the plates.
It felt a single toe. Who decided a fist counted for more?
If somebody stays down, do I keep counting?
When you have counted, go and sit beside him.
That's the part the clock on the wall can't do.
Your timer runs through the break between rounds.
We didn't record the rest periods.
Put them back in. A person has to breathe somewhere.
Who answers when all three of you are away?
A recording. We didn't want a stranger left waiting.
Leave a chair there. Someone may choose to stay.
The bell rang before either of us moved. Was that you?
Look at the knot in the rope. Somebody rang it yesterday and tied the sound inside.
Great. Whose scorecard does yesterday go on?

intro.text: That bell's got a dent in it.
Still makes a pretty good sound.
Let's see if I can get through without denting it again.

ending.text: I found the guy who kept answering the doors.
Thought he'd want a rematch. He wanted breakfast.
We had six bowls before he told me his name.
Next time I visit, I'm bringing my own spoon.

intro.text: This body remembers a thousand greetings.
How wasteful to offer them to strangers.
I shall decide which voice is worthy of it.

ending.text: I kept one perfect garden behind a sealed door.
Every flower turned toward the same light.
I called it harmony until I heard the bees on the other side.
I have yet to open it.

intro.text: Someone counted my home among his possessions.
Someone has made an elementary error.
Stand aside while I correct the arithmetic.

ending.text: They sent me a plaque for preserving their planet.
I turned it over. Perfectly good metal.
There's a new latch on the nursery window.
Let them puzzle over where their tribute went.

intro.text: I know how an order sounds inside one's own skull.
This one was careful to use my voice.
Even my imitation has better diction.

ending.text: The black seal left a scar across my palm.
I could wish the thing away. I keep it.
When some prince asks whether strength is worth any price, I open my hand.
He can do his own sums.

intro.text: My afternoon has developed a horizon where my soup should be.
I tolerate many things in a well-run universe.
Cold soup is not among them.

ending.text: Eight delegations came to negotiate for their continued existence.
I required one dish from each, served hot.
The eighth was dreadful. I let them try again.
An exceedingly generous interpretation of my duties.

intro.text: I had a lesson prepared.
Then the classroom got eaten.
Pop quiz, I guess.

ending.text: I put the bell on the lowest shelf at school.
First-year students get to ring it if I talk over them.
Terrible idea. They use it constantly.
I'm thinking of getting one for the faculty meetings.

intro.text: Every window here shows a slightly different street.
In one of them I'm still getting ready.
Tell that guy his shirt looks good.

ending.text: There's a minute left before my own street wants me back.
I spend it setting a timer on my students' camera.
Three terrible photos. In the fourth, everyone's laughing.
They can keep that one, whatever comes next.

intro.text: A harvest laid out for me.
How courteous of the farmer.
How unfortunate he stayed to eat.

ending.text: They offered the king a country of obedient mouths.
I let the first brave fool speak against me.
His voice shook. He got to finish.
A world is only worth taking if it can bare its teeth.

intro.text: I hear the breath that precedes a technique.
Even the door has learned to hold it.
Let's see where it exhales.

ending.text: I split the clasp from the wheel with a finger.
All those mouths began praying to the one who freed them.
I laughed. A useful lesson about gratitude.
The next prayer stopped halfway through my name.

intro.text: In my branch the feast ended long ago.
I remember the sound of the last bowl breaking.
Here they are still setting places.

ending.text: I took the empty seat nearest the kitchen.
The cook asked for payment before he served me.
So this is a world in which that sentence can still be spoken.
I gave him the emperor's coin. Let him find change.

intro.text: Before we begin, tell me your type.
That pause is a deeply unsettling answer.
Fine. Let your footwork answer for you.

ending.text: The first concert after the worlds went home sold out.
Eight doors. Eight queues. Everyone tried to cut in.
I spent the evening checking tickets and missed the first song.
A full house heard it. As a fan, I accept this result.

intro.text: Show me the seam.
Everybody else is staring at the light.
Things usually break at the ugly little joint.

ending.text: They wanted to put my weapon behind glass.
I said yes, if they'd leave the handle sticking out.
Some kid lifted it clean off the stand.
Museum lasted nine minutes. The training hall's still there.

intro.text: Funny place to get a job offer.
No advance. No expenses.
Guess I'll cut out the middleman.

ending.text: I found a bet slip tucked inside the wheel.
Eight worlds against one, with the money already down.
I tore the slip before I saw who held the other end.
For once nobody made a profit on the kid.

intro.text: Hey, can you feel your toes?
I know it's a weird question. Mine just went through the floor.
If yours are still here, help me pull.

ending.text: I stayed to put the seats back on the platform.
Found a glove. Then a kid with one cold hand.
He didn't know anything about the worlds that almost ended.
He said thanks for the glove. That part felt good.

intro.text: I've practised an introduction for emergencies.
Naturally I wrote it in the notebook I left at home.
Hi. Sword. Here to help.

ending.text: They asked what technique I used on the final door.
Actually, I held it for a woman pushing a stroller.
Then I held it for about two hundred other people.
My report says my arms were sore. My report is accurate.

intro.text: I can hear someone trying not to cry.
They think it'll make the door open wider.
It's all right. We'll hold it together.

ending.text: I went back to the place where the voices used to overlap.
One was still there. A little girl looking for her shoe.
She let me sit beside her until she found it herself.
I went home with two muddy knees and both hands empty.

intro.text: The shadow under that door is facing the light.
Don't let it get behind you.
I've had enough of things borrowing my shape.

ending.text: A dog sat at the last threshold and wouldn't budge.
Thought there was a curse. It was waiting for its person.
I waited too. Took most of the night.
Don't tell anybody I packed treats.

intro.text: The device has entered a plea on behalf of every living person.
I would like the record to show an objection.
I can handle the filing fee.

ending.text: I convened a hearing in the empty lab.
For once the accused was a procedure, not a person.
The remedy fit on a scrap of paper: ask again, and wait.
We posted it where the next engineer would see it.

intro.text: Who decided everybody has to go it alone?
Come on, I can hear you breathing in there.
Give me something to pull on!

ending.text: I asked every village to pick somebody to answer the bell.
A few picked the loudest kid they knew.
Finally, a job where nobody tells that kid to shut up.
I'll teach the first shift myself.

intro.text: There's a cut in the sky.
Someone's standing on the other side with my face.
He can wait his turn.

ending.text: I followed my own footprints back to the fork.
One trail carried on alone. The other had company.
I left a stone there so I'd remember where the choice was.
For the walk home I took the longer trail.

intro.text: Count the people before we close the opening.
I've lost enough time mistaking distance for duty.
I'll bring up the rear.

ending.text: There was room for one sentence on the last transmission.
I almost used it for coordinates.
I wrote that I would be home for dinner.
Then I made the necessary arrangements to be on time.

intro.text: A lie can sound very much like kindness.
I have experience with that error.
Please listen to the person I interrupted.

ending.text: The rift offered to rewrite what my brother knew.
I returned the offer unopened.
I had one minute to give him the whole truth.
Most of it I spent letting him finish his question.

intro.text: A seal that verifies its own maker. Sloppy.
Show me the hand that countersigned it.
If it's the same hand, we're starting over.

ending.text: I drafted a protocol requiring a witness from either shore.
My brother returned it with jam on the corner.
Underneath he'd written, 'Who speaks for the missing?'
I opened a fresh scroll. This one will take longer.

intro.text: Can you build a village in the time before a door closes?
Probably not. My brother will have estimates.
Let's start with somewhere for people to sit.

ending.text: We made benches from the wood left by the flood.
Opposite sides of the border, facing one another.
By spring someone had built a table in between.
I think that's the bit I like best.

intro.text: Mark the door on this side first.
Yes, I could get there faster.
I'd like the person behind me to get there too.

ending.text: They offered to name the rescue route after me.
I gave them a more practical name: way home.
Even a child lost in a crowd can read that arrow.
I put the first one down at a child's eye level.

intro.text: An empire with no one left to oppose it.
I've seen grander dreams in the minds of children.
Wake up and defend yours.

ending.text: In the last reflection my oldest friend was waiting at a river.
I could have stepped inside and made him agree with me forever.
Instead I threw him a stone. He threw it wide.
Even that small disappointment felt like him.

intro.text: A door that gives back whatever you've lost.
I know how much you want to believe it.
I know because I was holding it open.

ending.text: I went back to the minute I'd been buying.
This time I let the rain reach the ground.
There was no pardon waiting when the water cleared.
There was somebody beside me. We stood there getting wet.

intro.text: Hello! Authorized door inspector here!
Good news, the door opens!
Bad news, I appear to be the hinge.

ending.text: I left the mask on the handle when I went.
From the road it looked like someone still keeping watch.
I almost went back for it.
Let the empty face be the one that stays behind.

intro.text: Eight nations have heard one village scream.
For a moment they have something in common.
What shall they make of that moment?

ending.text: I took the chime to a street that had forgotten quiet.
When it rang, every household named somebody missing.
Nobody was asked to forgive.
For an evening the loudest country had to listen.

intro.text: My notes called for a picturesque entrance.
This ditch is picturesque from a very particular angle.
A hand, if you please.

ending.text: I had time for one more page before the water called me back.
Wrote an absolutely magnificent title.
Then I used the rest for the names of the kids who got out.
My editor can cut the title if he has to.

intro.text: Even a reflection of myself presumes to hold territory.
Stand and be measured.
I shall determine which of us casts the shadow.

ending.text: I returned to find a seed waiting in a bowl of dry earth.
It had all it required save a living world's assent.
I set the bowl before the nearest door and commanded it to open.
The seed remains in my possession. It grows no heavier.

intro.text: If you can talk, give me a count of the injured.
If you can't, squeeze my hand.
Good. You're first.

ending.text: I asked for volunteers to carry a stretcher across the last seam.
Got two dozen warriors and a great many opinions.
The patient chose who carried her.
That little clause is on every intake form now.

intro.text: My student would have rushed that opening.
At his age I might have done worse.
Watch once. Then show me another way.

ending.text: I brought the class two identical maps of the rift.
On one I marked the fastest passage.
They used the other one to bring an injured teammate through.
I gave the lesson back to them to teach next year.

intro.text: Someone behind us has stopped walking.
They're trying to be very quiet about it.
We can slow down.

ending.text: I marked the route with pieces of pale cloth.
People who couldn't see the far door could feel each knot.
At the last knot someone tied a ribbon of their own.
I left space on the cord for more.

intro.text: The sand is gathering around an empty patch of ground.
Someone was afraid there a moment ago.
Wait until they come through.

ending.text: I wanted to raise a wall around the scar in the village.
A child asked whether a wall could have a seat on top.
We built the seat first.
It's a favourite place to watch visitors arrive.

intro.text: Six bodies approach one threshold.
The threshold mistakes agreement for six witnesses.
Its arithmetic is corrupt.

ending.text: Six bells rang in a city of rain.
The machine heard six votes. It received one.
When the six bodies moved aside, another voice could be heard.
The petition of a single orphan stayed the harvest.

intro.text: There's a piece of string tied to the alarm.
Pretty sophisticated string, apparently.
Let's try the time-honoured method of looking up.

ending.text: I delivered my report and left a page blank.
Someone asked whether I'd forgotten to record the casualties.
No. For once I could leave that page blank.
I was on time getting it in. That's the truly improbable bit.

intro.text: Mask secure. Exit located.
One civilian occupying the exit.
Revising the route.

ending.text: The order said to destroy the last witness.
Turned out to be a recorder playing a child counting to ten.
I took it apart and delivered the tape to its owner.
The report says mission complete. It is.

intro.text: A gap like that won't care which side you're on.
Keep hold of the person next to you.
I'll watch the place where the hands disappear.

ending.text: We recovered a pair of goggles with one lens missing.
Through the good lens, the world was an ordinary dusty brown.
I set them on a stone facing the sunrise.
Someone else can decide what they mean.

intro.text: That building has a thousand people in it.
I don't care which universe stamped their papers.
Open the shelter.

ending.text: Every family got a key. Then somebody asked about visitors.
I'd been thinking like a man counting houses.
We built a guest room into the first public shelter.
I may use it myself when these meetings run late.

intro.text: It would be easy to make them turn away.
They might even thank me afterward.
Keep my hands in sight.

ending.text: One witness wanted the fear taken out of her memory.
I asked if she'd like a seat while she decided.
When the sun came up she wanted to keep the whole night.
I was glad I had waited.

intro.text: That squeak isn't a ghost. It's a loose bolt.
The scream immediately after it was me.
I know the difference, thank you!

ending.text: I heard one ordinary train whistle all the way home.
I stayed awake to hear it a second time.
Nobody around me understood why I was crying.
I told them I'd lost my ticket. That happened too.

intro.text: I count one more passenger than we have seats.
Take mine! I shall stand.
I have an exceptionally good grip!

ending.text: We brought the carriage to rest exactly where it was needed.
I had hoped for another meal before my stop.
A small hand passed me half a cold sweet potato.
I have had splendid meals. I remember this one.

intro.text: The bruising follows the thread, not the vein.
Hold still. This will sting a little.
That was your warning and my apology.

ending.text: I kept a vial of rain from the carriage window.
Under glass it proved to be ordinary water.
Imagine all the work we did for that plain little result.
I watered a sick patient's flowers with it.

intro.text: Which end of the mountain is its face?
It keeps biting from behind!
I'll just fight BOTH ends!

ending.text: I found the biggest mountain and challenged it again.
Echo yelled back, same voice as me.
We fought until sundown. I gave him half my dinner.
Stubborn guy never came down for it.

intro.text: [She taps the closed door twice, low enough for a child to reach.]
[A small fist taps back. She rests her cheek against the wood.]
[She plants both heels beside the hinge.]

ending.text: [At the last crossing she finds two sandals of very different sizes.]
[She sets them side by side. Two hands reach through for them.]
[A little while later the smaller hand comes back with a flower.]
[She carries it home upright between both palms.]

intro.text: Twelve dimensions and one extension cord.
Who rated this lab, a guy who sells extension cords?
Hand me the end that isn't screaming.

ending.text: I made a door that asks permission before it opens.
First time home, it kept me standing outside for forty minutes.
I had a perfectly good override in my pocket.
Used the forty minutes to think of something worth saying.

intro.text: My favourite part is when someone says it was an accident.
Takes real talent to build one this repeatable.
Hey, who's holding the receipt?

ending.text: I left them a spare door with my compliments.
Nobody opened it. A whole multiverse and no takers.
The box came back unopened, postage due.
Some jackass even spelled my name right.

intro.text: Is that a timer or does the universe just blink red now?
Either way, I know this part.
Little less staring, little more hero time.

ending.text: I put the little brass bell on my key ring.
Thought it would look cool next to the watch.
Yesterday somebody needed help and I couldn't transform.
Turns out the keys open the fire stairs just fine.

intro.text: Once again an inferior design dictates the shape I inhabit.
At least this inventor omitted the insufferable green trim.
I shall document the correction.

ending.text: For one hour the machine offered me any body I desired.
The invoice specified whose body would be taken in exchange.
I am a superior intellect. I do read the fine print.
I returned the apparatus. I kept the hour.

intro.text: It touched my car first.
I'm willing to work this out like reasonable people.
Reasonable people know what a new transmission costs.

ending.text: I welded the bell bracket onto the old dashboard.
Hit a pothole and it rings. Really annoying.
Then I picked up somebody stranded between two roads.
Guy told me he heard me coming. Guess it stays.

intro.text: The return spell has someone else's handwriting in the margin.
Don't trace it yet.
I want to see what word they crossed out.

ending.text: I copied the spell in a notebook with space between the lines.
Anyone who uses it has to write in their own destination.
First entry was a small, determined drawing of a house.
Worked on the first try.

intro.text: A machine that steals worlds one at a time.
An embarrassingly small ambition.
Kneel while I improve upon it.

ending.text: I took the wheel intact and mounted it on my flagship.
At my word a hundred doors opened on empty space.
The worlds themselves had chosen different coordinates.
My navigators have been instructed to omit this incident.

intro.text: I was literally on my way home.
I know. Everybody here was on their way somewhere.
Okay. Who needs a lift?

ending.text: I tried to explain the whole thing at dinner.
Mom asked about the kid with the drawing on his window.
I went back. He'd put a moon next to the sun.
That's the part I told her when I sat back down.

intro.text: An empire announces itself before it takes a world.
This one had the poor manners to borrow my son's voice.
I want to hear the recording.

ending.text: I taught the people of one planet how to recognize an imperial order.
Then I showed them where my signature appeared on theirs.
They asked me to leave. My feet did not want to move.
I left before they had to ask a second time.

intro.text: I ran the circumference of the block twice.
Same woman dropped the same bag both times.
This time I'm staying to pick up the oranges.

ending.text: I could have closed every shelter door in under a second.
One man was halfway through telling somebody goodbye.
I stood with my hand on the latch for twelve whole minutes.
His wife says I still shut it too fast.

intro.text: Emergency power draws from the signal itself.
Every time that lamp flashes we feed it.
Pass me the manual switch.

ending.text: I removed the master override from the cave.
Kept a mechanical release accessible from either side.
The first person to test it was a kid who couldn't reach.
I moved the handle down. That's the version we kept.

intro.text: That sunlight fell on my parents once.
Funny what you can miss without having a memory of it.
Let the light go. I'll hold the roof.

ending.text: A little boy offered me the paper sun from his window.
I told him about a red one I knew by other people's stories.
He drew that one on the back.
I've got two skies on my refrigerator now.

intro.text: Great. A cosmic keyhole.
I have exactly one arrow that might fit.
I'd appreciate a convincing gasp if this works.

ending.text: City hall wanted a heroic statue at the evacuation point.
I suggested an awning and a bench.
They had the nerve to put my name on the bench anyway.
Fine. At least you can sit on my legacy in the rain.

intro.text: My sensors say there's zero load on this bridge.
My knees have filed a minority report.
Everybody keep moving.

ending.text: I stripped the voiceprint lock out of the emergency system.
A hand crank works through a blackout and an alien invasion.
First kid who tested it yelled booyah.
I swear I didn't program that.

intro.text: We need somebody small enough to fit in there.
Okay. Small, brave, and emotionally prepared for lint.
I'm two out of three.

ending.text: There was a mouse family in the last crate.
The inventory listed it as empty. Rude.
I signed for all eleven with one little paw print each.
They ate the duplicates. Paperwork finally made sense.

intro.text: A thousand minds are afraid.
One of them keeps apologizing for the noise.
I'll sit with that one.

ending.text: I put a cushion in the room with the alarm.
People expect a prophecy when they come to sit there.
Mostly they get tea and a chance to finish a thought.
Some miracles benefit from a closed door.

intro.text: I am told this noise means welcome.
On my world a welcome usually permits a reply.
I have prepared a very loud one.

ending.text: I asked each shore to teach me its greeting.
One was a song. One involved a small respectful sneeze.
The final shore asked for a moment of quiet.
I have learned to say that one fluently.

intro.text: Sight lines first. Count the exits.
Somebody counted our exits for us.
That's the one we don't use.

ending.text: I gave each member of the team a different piece of the map.
They put it together and found a route I missed.
The debrief ran late because I let them argue it out.
I wrote their route in ink.

intro.text: What, nobody booked a camera?
There are holes in the sky and nobody booked a camera.
Fine. I'll give you time to find one.

ending.text: They put up a screen to replay the rescue.
Every time I came on, people turned to look at the actual sky.
I signed the screen for them.
Funny. Nobody's come to take it home.

intro.text: Cute little bell. We used to have air-raid sirens.
You heard one of those, you paid attention.
Look at that. Now I'm paying attention.

ending.text: They tried to hand me a commemorative uniform.
Didn't fit. Neither did the speech.
I took the last watch at the dock and lit a smoke.
Nobody clapped. Best damn shift all week.

intro.text: A seal holds while the hand stays true.
Somebody else wrote this one in my place.
I'll correct the last stroke.

ending.text: I signed the repair with my ordinary name.
The village returned it with a hundred small signatures.
The ink ran together when the rain came.
It held just the same.

intro.text: I learned my craft after hours.
Wonder how long it takes to learn a door that fights back.
Good thing I brought lunch.

ending.text: The homecoming feast needed another table.
Spent the afternoon cutting boards and slicing fish.
Nobody got to hear my big victory speech.
Second helpings got a much bigger cheer.

intro.text: Everybody waiting for a brilliant plan?
Hang on. Had it a second ago.
You get us through the door. I'll improvise the brilliant part.

ending.text: I tried to surprise the next patrol with a shortcut.
They surprised me by following my chalk marks.
For once the clever bit was telling people where I'd gone.
I'm keeping the chalk.

intro.text: We have eyes on both sides.
Count us in together.
The last one through gets the same welcome as the first.

ending.text: We put the roll call on a card by the door.
At first it had only our team on it.
The next shift pencilled in everyone who swept the floor afterward.
We had to get a bigger card.

intro.text: Civilians clear. Squad present.
That signal uses a stolen badge.
We intend to recover it in person.

ending.text: We logged the stolen orders as evidence.
Every person named in them received a copy and a chance to reply.
The case file got heavy enough to need two people.
We carried it together.

intro.text: The echo is one beat late.
Listen for the foot that lands between the bells.
That's the real opening.

ending.text: We put an echo at the crossing to demonstrate the escape route.
It could show the steps. It couldn't take anyone's hand.
We started sending a living guide with it.
Turned out to be a pretty good double act.

intro.text: Hear that low note? Whole herd felt it.
Give us room for the wings.
We'll clear the ground together.

ending.text: We found our prints in the mud by the breach.
One set looked huge. Another barely touched down.
Kids made casts before the rain could wash them out.
Four different tracks. One direction.

intro.text: Three winds just met in a school hallway.
Anybody got a broom?
Right. Save the school, then sweep.

ending.text: We promised the caretaker we'd fix the courtyard.
Nobody mentioned how many leaves fit inside a whirlwind.
The last bag took until dark.
Next time we're opening the doors before practice.

intro.text: Hear the wind under the floor?
You take the upper opening.
We'll have somebody waiting below.

ending.text: We ran the relay forward until every kid could get out.
Then we ran it backward to see who we'd missed.
Found the caretaker going back for a class photograph.
We brought both through.

intro.text: Unit present.
Awaiting authorization.
Conflicting command: protect occupant.

ending.text: Last order received: hold door.
Contact sensor reports small hand on frame.
Order maintained until contact sensor clears.
Duration: as long as required.

intro.text: The bell sounds twice before the striker moves.
Good. Something quicker than these old eyes.
May I have another look?

ending.text: I set a bell on a low table and challenged the youngest visitor.
She covered it with both hands so neither of us could ring it.
A draw! The most economical technique I've seen in years.
I bowed first. She made quite sure of that.

intro.text: The guy who laid this trap wants us to hurry.
So take a break. Here, chocolate.
Okay. Now we can hurry.

ending.text: I took the scenic exit because nobody had ordered me to.
Found an old vending machine with one candy bar left.
I broke it exactly in half and wrapped one piece for later.
It's a better reason to go home than being called.

intro.text: A threshold where strong things gather.
And someone has carelessly left the latch undone.
What a sweet sound.

ending.text: I stuck a playing card over the hairline crack.
Someday perhaps a worthy hand will push it through.
This morning it fell neatly into my lap.
Wind, they say. I have packed my things anyway.

intro.text: Eight stolen worlds and no catalogue.
The thief lacks affection for his collection.
I would like to browse.

ending.text: In the ruins I found a book with every page blank.
Its owner said the missing names were still his to remember.
I left it on the shelf. That surprised him.
I took the shelf from under it. That surprised him too.

intro.text: I heard the sky thinking. It wants my Saturday.
I already promised my Saturday to a dessert cup.
This had better be quick.

ending.text: I restored the table where I'd left my coffee jelly.
One spoon missing. Seven friends suddenly available.
An unprecedented number of volunteers offered to share.
I went back through the door for seven more spoons.

intro.text: You can look away if the shield flickers.
Actually, keep looking.
I'd like somebody to tell me when it holds.

ending.text: I built a little privacy screen around the last reunion.
No cameras, no questions, just two people hugging.
I could have disappeared too.
I stayed until they asked to come out.

intro.text: Race you to the crack in the sky!
Oh. It's getting closer on its own.
Okay, race you AWAY from the crack in the sky!

ending.text: I delivered every missing shoe in the lost-and-found.
I even matched the lefts and rights.
There's one kid who wants to race me now that he has both.
I'm giving him the inside lane. He's pretty quick.

intro.text: Every great rescue needs a really excellent crisis.
Usually I'd take that as a compliment.
Who took my control panel?

ending.text: I designed a rescue beacon small enough for any kid's pocket.
The first production run had my face on the button.
A kid kept pressing my nose until the paint wore off.
She got through every time. I approved the second run.

intro.text: Somebody put a tropical sea through a subway turnstile.
I've had evenings like this.
Not many of them ended in dry shoes.

ending.text: I laid an ice path across the last flooded platform.
Came back next day. A little girl was standing there with skates.
She'd been promised another go when it got cold.
I had ten minutes. The ice held for eleven.

intro.text: That beam is carrying two ceilings.
I can handle the beam.
Would somebody mind handling the people looking up at it?

ending.text: Afterward we tried to lift a dining table through our front door.
I'd just held up a whole building. The table got stuck.
We took the legs off and all carried a piece.
We ate at that table tonight.

intro.text: Everybody grab a hand. Yours counts too, sweetheart.
I can stretch pretty far.
I still need to know when you've got hold.

ending.text: We checked every shelter twice.
At the last one a kid asked who was checking on the parents.
That's how we ended up with six kids running the welcome desk.
We signed in like everybody else.

intro.text: There's a phone ringing in a room you've never seen.
Aren't you the least bit curious who has the number?
Go on. Say hello.

ending.text: I called every house on the block at midnight.
Every house picked up. Nobody said a word.
Then my own phone started ringing.
I let it go to voicemail. There are limits.

intro.text: [One wet boot comes down across the seam.]
[The bell rope winds around his wrist. He looks at it.]
[He pulls once. The post comes out of the ground.]

ending.text: [He walks into the water carrying the last length of chain.]
[The light under the dock sinks with him.]
[On shore the phone rings until its battery dies.]
[A ripple touches the steps. Nothing follows it out.]

intro.text: I can hear someone on the wrong side of that wall.
Don't care what department it's supposed to be.
I'm going through.

ending.text: One soul was afraid to cross because nobody knew her name.
I sat on the curb and let her tell me how to spell it.
She went on ahead. The street was boring again.
I wrote it inside my schoolbook before I forgot.

intro.text: Sometimes I miss the turn and find a better fight.
Looks like this is one of those times.
Go on. You pick the direction.

ending.text: I chased the last bell until the sound ran out.
Wound up in the same square I'd left three days before.
Whole crowd there wanted to hear where I'd been.
I pointed. They started laughing. It was the wrong way again.

intro.text: Hear that scrape? She's awake.
A world this wide ought to give her room.
Get behind me if you like your roof.

ending.text: We came to a piece of the wheel still too big for the gate.
Took one cut. Everybody watched the iron fall in two.
I waited for the sound underneath it.
Good. I can still hear her.

intro.text: An experiment that eats its control group.
I object on strictly professional grounds.
Hand me the surviving variable.

ending.text: I preserved one sample of the silence between worlds.
Every time I measured it, it contained the apparatus instead.
A mediocre researcher might find this humbling.
I billed the apparatus for wasting my time.

intro.text: Those names are written in the hand of no living clerk.
Yet the bereaved have treated them as law.
I will hear their petition.

ending.text: One soul returned without the seal required for passage.
I signed as her witness in my own hand.
The clerk asked what precedent he should record.
Record that she arrived.

intro.text: I followed a flyer for a free exhibition.
Exhibiting what, exactly?
The little map had a cup on it.

ending.text: The prize was one paper cup of fruit punch.
I won the safety deposit back by returning the cup.
On the way home a kid wanted to know how hard I'd hit.
Didn't have to. Pretty good deal, actually.

intro.text: Recording vibration at both ends of the room.
A third signal arrived without crossing the space between.
Requesting permission to intervene immediately.

ending.text: I charted each victory against total energy expended.
The deciding action barely registered on the graph.
I wrote 'listened' in the empty column.
Sensei put a drink on the page. I preserved the ring as data.

intro.text: Someone has obtained the power to decide who is spared.
The obvious question is who supervises its use.
I would like to see the register.

ending.text: I drew up a list of people qualified to answer for the world.
It took me hours to reduce it to a single name.
The door required the signature of someone besides me.
I still have the pen.

intro.text: I estimate a high probability that this door is lying.
The cake on the far side is a particularly crude inducement.
I shall require a fork to test it.

ending.text: I filed the case under a question mark.
It bothered the archivist, who asked for a more useful title.
I asked what they would have called it.
The new folder reads 'Everyone Came Home.' A provisional conclusion.

intro.text: Eight universes, one city bus in the middle of the intersection.
My stop, apparently.
Anybody here know how to release a parking brake?

ending.text: I got the bus back on its route six hours late.
A lady gave me a transfer slip so I could ride home.
Couldn't exactly explain the whole swinging thing.
Sat by a window. She pointed out her favourite rooftops.

intro.text: I can feel the dock moving under my shoes.
It's a little like coming home on the boat.
Keep my knees soft. I can do this.

ending.text: I took the bell to the gym. They let me ring the first round.
The sound was ordinary again. Made my hands shake anyway.
A new kid asked if being strong meant that would stop.
I held the rope for him. I told him I was still finding out.

intro.text: I was headed for the kitchen.
This sea wasn't here a minute ago.
Somebody moved the kitchen.

ending.text: I cut a straight passage across the folded maps.
Everybody else reached the ship before supper.
I found a little island nobody knew was missing.
Who says taking a turn costs you time?

intro.text: At last, an entrance on an appropriate scale!
Wait. Which side of the entrance am I on?
Get my feet back here before the applause!

ending.text: They put up a poster of the pirate who held eight worlds together.
I'd have preferred a better angle, but the nose came out fine.
I sold souvenir copies until the tide turned.
Then I noticed somebody was selling souvenirs of me selling souvenirs.

intro.text: I can smell a galley behind that wall.
Butter's browning. Somebody left in a hurry.
If we're fighting, make it quick.

ending.text: I cooked from what each shore could spare.
Eight pots, eight fires, one last hungry passenger.
He tried to pay with a coin from a world that no longer used it.
I gave him change. A packed lunch for tomorrow.

intro.text: Funny how the word toll sounds different from this side of a gate.
I don't care for the sound.
I intend to stand on the other side again.

ending.text: They offered my people a passage and handed me the key.
I saw who was waiting to collect on the far bank.
I crushed the key before they could set a price.
That sea owes nobody a coin. Especially them.

intro.text: The sky's got a mouth!
Think it eats meat?
Hey! That's OUR meat!

ending.text: I rang the bell and heard eight people asking what I wanted.
Dinner! Guess what, they all made something different.
We pushed the tables through while the doors were still open.
Now the map has a great big grease mark where my favourite place is.

intro.text: That little click before the alarm is my screwdriver slipping.
I built an entire disaster on half a turn of a screw.
Hand it back. I'm staying for the repair.

ending.text: I put the first invitation in an envelope and walked it across town.
Ridiculous time to spend on a distance my machine could fold.
Dseyl opened the door with flour all over both hands.
We were halfway through dinner before we talked about the lab.

intro.text: I can tell which door you used by the pitch of its hinge.
This one has two pitches and no bottom screw.
Stand clear while I put my shoulder to it.

ending.text: I took apart the wheel for the metal.
The good brass made eighty small bells, each with a different pitch.
You could tell whose door you were at without lifting your head.
I kept the ugly one that sounds like home.

intro.text: I keep the lab's log. In pencil, these days.
The ink kept making guesses look official.
Tell me exactly what you heard.

ending.text: I wrote the whole trip down, then passed the book around.
A hundred hands crossed things out. One kid drew his shoe.
It's twice as thick and there's jam in the binding.
It's the first accurate account we've got.

intro.text: There is room beside me.
You need not tell me first what brought you here.
Come and see who else is waiting.

ending.text: At the last door a man asked how much bread was left.
He had been last in line each time the world began again.
I sat beside him and broke the loaf in my hands.
He took the first piece to the woman behind the counter.

intro.text: That thing presses down like a hand on the back of my neck.
I know that feeling from the dinner table.
Let's see if it knows mine.

ending.text: I set out two bowls of rice and waited for a fight.
The only visitor was a kid who wanted to practise his stance.
The rice went cold while we worked on his left foot.
We ate it anyway. That was a pretty good fight.

speech.text: I held your little bell to my ear. A woman was asking if her son had eaten.
Beyond her kitchen I could taste the life of an entire world.
Your machine offered me that world for the weight of one recorded breath.
I have emptied skies for less. I remember the sound her spoon made when it fell.
Now you would have me wait on her doorstep until she answers for herself.
Very well. Ring once. Let us see whose hand she finds when she opens the door.

naruto.text: You used to paint your name where everyone could see. Have you learned what it costs to put it under an order?

naruto_seventh.text: Seventh Hokage. Try closing one hand around all the little hands that reach for yours.

sasuke.text: You count the exits before you look me in the eye. Sensible. I have counted them too.

sasuke_adult.text: You remember what it costs to get one boy home. How many worlds would you spend for a second chance?

sasuke_sensei.text: You taught a child to watch the hand behind the blow. Have you warned them about yours?

omololu.text: I kept the very first sound you gave me, Omololu. You took a breath as if about to say somebody's name.

gojo.text: Six Eyes, and you spent your first glance on the child behind me. Such an expensive habit.

gojo_shinjuku.text: Dressed for the decisive hour, I see. How inconvenient that a stranger needs another minute.

goku.text: You are watching my feet. Even here, some part of you is simply pleased to meet a difficult opponent.

halfHealth.text: They're answering out of time. Who taught them to do that?

defeat.text: One kitchen. One spoon. How can there still be someone there to pick it up?

narration.text: A brass bell came home with a dent a thumb could find in the dark.
The first voice to answer it belonged to a woman at a stove.
She had warmed the same bowl three times. This time her son came in.
Across the worlds, the people who carried the call went back to their unfinished days.
At the lab, three chairs stood beside the door. That evening two were occupied.
The third was for whoever knocked.
